name: Narrative Architecture
description: Forty-eight story-structure patterns for turning a change into something an audience can follow, believe and act on.

rules.title: Narrative Architecture Rules
rules.intro:
Apply these rules when shaping a change into a story an audience can follow.
Each card names one structure, the beats that make it work, and where it fails.

skill.name: narrative
skill.description: Structure a talk, proposal or case study against the Narrative Architecture deck — {cards} story patterns. Use when a message needs a shape: a pitch, an incident write-up, an executive brief, a launch. Start with the index below, then read the one resource file for the family you are shaping.
skill.title: Narrative Architecture
skill.intro:
This file is the index. The cards themselves live in `resources/`, one
file per family. Use the tables below to decide which file to open, then
read that file. Do not load every resource unless the change spans several
families.
commonRules:
Write the beats before choosing words; a structure that is not visible in
  the order of the material is not the structure.

One structure per piece. A second one competes with the first for the same
  attention.

The audience's change is the spine: say what they believed before, and what
  they should believe after.
skill.footer: Every card cites a primary source or names the tradition it comes from; the citation travels with the card.
